## XSS

### FG-XSS-001

**Dynamic innerHTML/outerHTML assignment** · `no-inner-html` · default severity: **high** · CWE-79 · A03:2021 - Injection

Assigning a dynamic value to innerHTML or outerHTML parses it as HTML, which executes injected markup and scripts.

**How to fix:** Use textContent for text. If you must render HTML, sanitize it first (e.g. DOMPurify.sanitize) or use the Trusted Types API.

### FG-XSS-002

**Dynamic code execution** · `no-eval` · default severity: **critical** · CWE-95 · A03:2021 - Injection

eval(), new Function() and string arguments to setTimeout/setInterval compile strings as code, turning any injected value into code execution.

**How to fix:** Remove eval and new Function. Parse data with JSON.parse and pass functions, not strings, to timers.

### FG-XSS-003

**document.write() call** · `no-document-write` · default severity: **high** · CWE-79 · A03:2021 - Injection

document.write() and document.writeln() inject raw HTML into the page and are a classic XSS sink.

**How to fix:** Build DOM nodes with createElement/append or let your framework render them.

### FG-XSS-004

**React dangerouslySetInnerHTML** · `no-dangerously-set-inner-html` · default severity: **high** · CWE-79 · A03:2021 - Injection

dangerouslySetInnerHTML bypasses React escaping. Any untrusted data that reaches __html is executed as markup.

**How to fix:** Render text through JSX. If raw HTML is unavoidable, pass it through DOMPurify.sanitize before setting __html.

### FG-XSS-005

**Vue v-html directive** · `no-v-html` · default severity: **high** · CWE-79 · A03:2021 - Injection

v-html renders raw HTML and executes any markup injected into the bound value.

**How to fix:** Use text interpolation ({{ }}). If raw HTML is required, sanitize it with DOMPurify before binding.

### FG-XSS-006

**Angular sanitizer bypass** · `no-bypass-security-trust` · default severity: **critical** · CWE-79 · A03:2021 - Injection

DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrust* disables the built-in Angular XSS protection for that value.

**How to fix:** Let Angular sanitize bindings automatically. If you must trust a value, sanitize it with DOMPurify first and keep the bypass in one audited place.

### FG-XSS-007

**Dynamic HTML passed to a parsing API** · `no-html-sink-call` · default severity: **high** · CWE-79 · A03:2021 - Injection

insertAdjacentHTML, Range.createContextualFragment and setHTMLUnsafe parse their argument as HTML, executing injected markup.

**How to fix:** Insert text with insertAdjacentText/textContent, or sanitize the HTML with DOMPurify (or Element.setHTML) first.

### FG-XSS-008

**javascript: URL** · `no-javascript-url` · default severity: **medium** · CWE-79 · A03:2021 - Injection

javascript: URLs run code when followed. They are a common XSS vector in href, src and form actions.

**How to fix:** Use event handlers for behaviour, and validate user-supplied URLs against an allowlist of schemes (https:, mailto:).

### FG-XSS-009

**Svelte {@html} tag** · `no-svelte-html` · default severity: **high** · CWE-79 · A03:2021 - Injection

{@html ...} inserts raw HTML without escaping and executes injected markup.

**How to fix:** Render values with normal {expressions}. If raw HTML is required, sanitize it with DOMPurify first.

### FG-XSS-010

**Navigation to a URL taken from the page address** · `no-open-redirect` · default severity: **high** · CWE-601 · A01:2021 - Broken Access Control

A value read from location.search/hash, URLSearchParams, document.referrer or window.name is used as a navigation target. Attackers craft links that redirect victims to phishing pages, or run code with a javascript: URL (DOM-based XSS).

**How to fix:** Only redirect to relative paths you validate (e.g. must start with "/" and not "//"), or to an allow-list of origins checked with new URL(value, location.origin).origin.

### FG-XSS-011

**Code-executing attribute set from a dynamic value** · `no-dangerous-attribute` · default severity: **high** · CWE-79 · A03:2021 - Injection

Event-handler attributes (onclick, onerror...) are compiled as JavaScript and iframe srcdoc is parsed as a full HTML document, so a dynamic value there executes injected code. URL attributes fed from the page address accept javascript: URLs.

**How to fix:** Attach handlers with addEventListener and a function, render iframe content from a sanitized string (DOMPurify) or a separate URL, and validate URLs against an allow-list of protocols (https:, mailto:).

### FG-XSS-012

**Prototype pollution in object merge** · `no-prototype-pollution` · default severity: **high** · CWE-1321 · A08:2021 - Software and Data Integrity Failures

A merge/extend/set helper copies attacker-controllable keys onto an object without rejecting "__proto__", "constructor" and "prototype". A payload such as {"__proto__": {...}} then adds properties to every object on the page, which turns into DOM XSS through sanitizers and templating (DOMPurify CVE-2026-41238) or code execution on the server (React2Shell, CVE-2025-55182).

**How to fix:** Skip "__proto__", "constructor" and "prototype" keys (or check Object.hasOwn(source, key)), merge into Object.create(null) or a Map, or use structuredClone / a maintained library such as lodash.merge >= 4.6.2.

## Secrets

### FG-SEC-001

**AWS credentials exposed** · `no-aws-credentials` · default severity: **critical** · CWE-798 · A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures

AWS access keys or secret keys were found in source code. They grant direct access to AWS services and can lead to full account compromise.

**How to fix:** Remove the credentials, rotate them in the AWS console and load them at runtime from a secrets manager. Never ship AWS credentials to the browser.

### FG-SEC-002

**API key or token exposed** · `no-api-tokens` · default severity: **high** · CWE-798 · A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures

A provider API key or token was found hardcoded in source code. Anything bundled into frontend code is readable by every visitor.

**How to fix:** Remove the key, rotate it in the provider dashboard and call the provider from your backend instead. Browser-safe keys (e.g. Google Maps) must be restricted by HTTP referrer.

### FG-SEC-003

**Private key exposed** · `no-private-keys` · default severity: **critical** · CWE-321 · A02:2021 - Cryptographic Failures

A private cryptographic key (RSA, EC, DSA, PGP or OpenSSH) was found.

**How to fix:** Remove the key from version control, revoke and regenerate it, and keep it in a vault.

### FG-SEC-004

**Hardcoded JWT** · `no-hardcoded-jwt` · default severity: **high** · CWE-798 · A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures

A JSON Web Token was found in source code. JWTs carry identity claims and are often still valid when leaked.

**How to fix:** Remove the token. Obtain tokens at runtime through your authentication flow and keep them in httpOnly cookies.

### FG-SEC-005

**Database connection string exposed** · `no-connection-strings` · default severity: **critical** · CWE-798 · A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures

A database URL containing credentials was found in source code.

**How to fix:** Remove the connection string, rotate the password and keep database access on the server.

### FG-SEC-006

**High-entropy string** · `no-high-entropy-strings` · default severity: **medium** · CWE-798 · A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures

A long random-looking string was found. It may be a credential; review it and suppress the finding if it is not.

**How to fix:** If the string is a credential, move it out of the code. Otherwise add `// frontguard-ignore-next-line FG-SEC-006` above it.

### FG-SEC-007

**Server secret exposed through a public env variable** · `no-secret-in-public-env` · default severity: **high** · CWE-200 · A01:2021 - Broken Access Control

Variables prefixed with NEXT_PUBLIC_, VITE_, REACT_APP_, NUXT_PUBLIC_, PUBLIC_, EXPO_PUBLIC_... are inlined into the JavaScript sent to the browser. A name like VITE_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY or NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_SECRET means a server secret is readable by every visitor.

**How to fix:** Rename the variable without the public prefix, read it only in server code (API routes, server actions, load functions), and rotate the secret: it is already in your deployed bundles.

## Auth

### FG-AUTH-001

**Auth token stored in Web Storage** · `no-token-in-web-storage` · default severity: **high** · CWE-922 · A04:2021 - Insecure Design

localStorage and sessionStorage are readable by any script on the page, so a single XSS bug leaks every token stored there.

**How to fix:** Keep session tokens in httpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies. If the token must live in JS, keep it in memory and make it short-lived.

### FG-AUTH-002

**Credential passed in a URL** · `no-token-in-url` · default severity: **high** · CWE-598 · A04:2021 - Insecure Design

Tokens in query strings end up in browser history, server and proxy logs, and Referer headers.

**How to fix:** Send credentials in the Authorization header or in the request body.

### FG-AUTH-003

**Hardcoded credential** · `no-hardcoded-credentials` · default severity: **critical** · CWE-798 · A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures

A password or secret is assigned as a string literal. Everything in frontend code ships to the browser and can be read by anyone.

**How to fix:** Remove the credential. Authenticate through your backend and load server-side secrets from the environment.

### FG-AUTH-004

**Math.random() used for a security value** · `no-insecure-random` · default severity: **medium** · CWE-338 · A02:2021 - Cryptographic Failures

Math.random() is not cryptographically secure: its output can be predicted from a few samples. Tokens, nonces, OAuth state, PKCE verifiers, salts or passwords generated with it can be guessed.

**How to fix:** Use crypto.getRandomValues() or crypto.randomUUID() (available in every browser and in Node), e.g. crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32)).

### FG-AUTH-005

**Auth cookie written from JavaScript** · `no-insecure-cookie` · default severity: **medium** · CWE-1004 · A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration

A session or token cookie is set through document.cookie. Cookies written by JavaScript can never be httpOnly, so any XSS can read them, and without Secure and SameSite they also travel over plain HTTP and cross-site requests.

**How to fix:** Let the server set auth cookies with Set-Cookie: name=value; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax (or Strict). If a cookie must be set in JS, add "; Secure; SameSite=Strict" and keep secrets out of it.

## Misconfiguration

### FG-CFG-001

**Public source maps in build config** · `no-public-sourcemaps` · default severity: **medium** · CWE-540 · A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration

Publishing source maps exposes your original source code, comments and internal paths to anyone.

**How to fix:** Use "hidden" source maps (uploaded to your error tracker but not served), or disable them for production builds.

### FG-CFG-002

**Insecure http:// or ws:// resource** · `no-mixed-content` · default severity: **medium** · CWE-319 · A02:2021 - Cryptographic Failures

Loading scripts, data or sockets over plain HTTP/WS lets anyone on the network read or tamper with them, and browsers block it on HTTPS pages.

**How to fix:** Use https:// and wss:// URLs for every resource and API endpoint.

### FG-CFG-003

**Third-party resource without Subresource Integrity** · `require-sri` · default severity: **low** · CWE-353 · A08:2021 - Software and Data Integrity Failures

A script or stylesheet is loaded from another origin without an integrity hash. If that host is compromised, its code runs on your page.

**How to fix:** Add integrity="sha384-..." and crossorigin="anonymous" to the tag, or self-host the file.

### FG-CFG-004

**postMessage with "*" target origin** · `no-wildcard-postmessage` · default severity: **medium** · CWE-345 · A01:2021 - Broken Access Control

postMessage(data, "*") delivers the message to whatever origin the target window currently has, leaking data to attacker-controlled frames.

**How to fix:** Pass the exact origin you expect, e.g. postMessage(data, "https://app.example.com").

### FG-CFG-005

**message event handler without an origin check** · `require-message-origin-check` · default severity: **medium** · CWE-346 · A01:2021 - Broken Access Control

A window "message" listener reads the event without checking event.origin. Any site that can open or frame your page can post messages to it, so the data must be treated as attacker-controlled (DOM XSS, token theft, CSRF-style actions).

**How to fix:** Return early unless event.origin matches the exact origin you expect (if (event.origin !== "https://app.example.com") return;), and validate the shape of event.data before using it.

### FG-CFG-006

**Dev server protections disabled** · `no-exposed-dev-server` · default severity: **medium** · CWE-942 · A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration

The dev server accepts any Host header, any CORS origin or serves files outside the project. Any website you visit can then read your source and files such as .env through your local dev server (DNS rebinding and cross-origin reads, as in the Vite file-read CVEs CVE-2025-30208, CVE-2025-31125 and CVE-2025-24010).

**How to fix:** Keep the defaults: list exact hostnames in server.allowedHosts, leave server.fs.strict enabled and cors restricted to known origins. Keep Vite and webpack-dev-server up to date.

## Dependencies

### FG-DEP-001

**Vulnerable dependency** · `no-vulnerable-dependencies` · default severity: **high** · CWE-1395 · A06:2021 - Vulnerable and Outdated Components

An installed package version has a published security advisory (source: OSV.dev).

**How to fix:** Upgrade the package to a patched version, or replace it.
